messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Government, political systems and organisations, Political behaviour and attitudes, and Political ideology in Germany during the 2020s, matching this research need: Representative telephone survey data on German-speaking residents aged 14+ in Germany, February 2024, about the Ukraine war, crisis perceptions, and related public opinion trends.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: Februar 2024 repräsentative Telefonbefragung deutschsprachige Bevölkerung ab 14 Jahren Ukraine Krieg Krisen Wahrnehmung Datensatz
February 2024 German speaking population 14 years telephone survey Ukraine war crises survey dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Krisenmonitor (Woche 8/2024) / Crisis Monitor (Week 8/2024) — GESIS Study ZA8738","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.14353","justification":"Exact match to the research need. This representative telephone survey (CATI) was conducted by forsa from February 19–21, 2024, among German-speaking residents aged 14 and older in Germany. Commissioned by the Press and Information Office of the German Federal Government, it examines public perceptions of ongoing crises, personal concerns about developments in Germany, political disagreements, democratic participation, perceived conflicts between political and social groups, and attitudes toward democracy. It belongs to the Crisis Monitor series, which continues the Ukraine War Trend Questions surveys initiated in March 2022. The dataset is particularly suitable for investigating political attitudes, crisis perceptions, democratic values, political polarization, and changes in German public opinion in the context of the Ukraine war. Available through the GESIS Data Archive under study identifier ZA8738."},{"title":"Krisenmonitor (Woche 8/2024) / Crisis Monitor (Week 8/2024) — B2FIND Dataset Record","url_or_doi":"https://b2find.eudat.eu/dataset/86168a1c-51c7-5399-a5d3-206519a07ded","justification":"Alternative discovery record for the exact February 2024 dataset, providing detailed German-language metadata about the survey population, telephone interview methodology, collection dates, and questionnaire topics. The record documents questions about personal experiences of current crises, political disputes, democratic engagement, perceived threats to democracy, and ideological conflicts between political groups. Particularly useful for verifying the dataset's suitability for research on government, political systems, political behaviour, political attitudes, and political ideology in Germany. This is the same underlying survey as GESIS ZA8738, not an independent sample."},{"title":"Krisenmonitor (Woche 16/2024) / Crisis Monitor (Week 16/2024)","url_or_doi":"https://b2find.eudat.eu/dataset/983d6b3f-f7bb-5519-b900-0ddc0085cff9","justification":"Highly relevant follow-up survey from the same Crisis Monitor series, conducted April 18–22, 2024, using telephone interviews with German-speaking residents aged 14 and older. Although collected after the requested February period, it provides complementary information on public anxiety about the Ukraine war, perceptions of responsibility for the Russia–Ukraine conflict, attitudes toward negotiations, evaluations of Germany's response to the Russian invasion, and opinions about Western sanctions. Suitable for examining changes in crisis perceptions and foreign-policy attitudes during 2024."},{"title":"Trendfragen Ukraine (Woche 48/2022) / Ukraine War Trend Questions (Week 48/2022) — GESIS Study ZA7924","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7924?lang=en","justification":"Relevant historical comparison dataset from the predecessor series to the 2024 Crisis Monitor. Conducted November 28–30, 2022, through representative computer-assisted telephone interviews with German-speaking residents aged 14 and older. The survey examines public attitudes toward Germany and the Ukraine war. It uses the same target population and general survey approach as the February 2024 Crisis Monitor, making it useful for longitudinal comparisons of public opinion about the war and related political developments. Questionnaire differences should be checked before conducting trend analyses."}]}
